chunks: Abu Sulayman narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Hammad narrated to us, from Amr ibn Shamar, who said:

I was with Abu Abdillah in his house, and the house was crowded with his family. The people came to him asking questions, and he answered whatever they asked about. I began to cry from one side of the house. He said: 'What is making you cry, O Amr?' I said: 'May I be your ransom, how can I not cry? Is there anyone like you in this ummah, while the door is closed upon you and the curtain is lowered over you?' He said: 'Do not cry, O Amr. We eat the good foods and wear the soft clothes. If what you say were true, we would only eat coarse food and wear rough clothes, like Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib; otherwise, it is being treated with shackles in Hell.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib)

ai.seo_question: Why did Amr ibn Shamar cry when seeing Imam al-Sadiq in his home, and what was the Imam's response?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the theological concept of *al-ghaybah al-sughra* (Minor Occultation), where Imam al-Sadiq (as) reassures Amr ibn Shamar that his relative comfort is not hypocrisy but a divine dispensation. The Imam contrasts this with the extreme asceticism of Imam Ali (as), implying that if the Imams were truly stripped of status, they would live in hardship; thus, their current ease is a sign of God's favor rather than a cause for weeping or divine punishment.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (8) Abu Sulayman narrated from Ibraheem bin Iss’haq from Abdullah bin Hammad that Amr bin Shimr had said:

Once I was with Abu Abdullah as-Sadiq (as) in his house. The house was crowded of people. They began to ask about different things. Whatever he was asked about something, he gave the sufficient answer. I began to cry. He asked: “O Amr, why are you crying?” I said: “May I die for you! How do I not cry? Is there any other one like you in this umma? You are imprisoned here, the door is closed and the curtain is lowered before you!” He said: “O Amr, do not cry! We eat good foods and wear soft cloths. If what you say occurs, we will eat coarse foods and wear rough cloths like Amirul Mo’mineen Ali bin Abu Talib (as); otherwise putting on ties in Hell.”
